items.label: Slide 2 ('What the module must hand back: one JSON report, no model')
items.focus: Define the deliverable and how success is measured.
deepseek_issues: The five success-criteria chips are bare labels ('Real files', 'All keys filled', 'Reproducible', 'No training'), so the slide's stated point — how success is measured — is never actually taught. A beginner cannot know what 'Reproducible' or 'All keys filled' requires. Fix: give each chip a one-line gloss underneath, e.g. '1 · Real files — reads the actual results.csv + images, not stand-ins'; '2 · ≤ 8 images — at most 8 leaf photos opened'; '3 · All keys filled — every field present, none empty'; '4 · Reproducible — a rerun gives the same numbers'; '5 · No training — the pipeline never fits a classifier'.

The field 'class_balance_min / max — 13 / 14' is not explained and reads like a fraction (0.93). A beginner cannot tell these are the smallest and largest per-class counts, or how to obtain them. Fix: annotate it as 'class_balance_min / max — 13 and 14 (smallest and largest number of photos in any one class)'.
deepseek_polish: The 'image_profiles' annotation 'per-image measurements' is too vague to define a deliverable; name the actual fields, e.g. 'image_profiles — width, height, mean RGB per sampled image'.
'risky_classes — lowest-F1 classes (least precision + recall)' has awkward wording; write 'risky_classes — the three classes with the lowest F1 (weakest on both precision and recall)'.

The JSON block is small at projector scale with two dense columns; consider raising the font size and grouping fields (counts / classes / sample / scores) so the two-column annotations do not sit so close together.

The code-block-plus-two-panels arrangement repeats the look of the earlier results.csv slide; making the five acceptance checks the dominant visual (a large numbered checklist with pass criteria, JSON block secondary) would differentiate the slide and better match its 'how we measure success' purpose.
Capitalisation in the chips is inconsistent ('≤ 8 Images' vs 'Real files'); lowercase 'images' for consistency.

items.label: Slide 5 ('Method 1b: From Pixels to Candidate Blobs')
items.focus: The threshold gives scattered pixels; connected-component labelling groups them into countable blobs, and an area filter throws away noise.
deepseek_issues: The three step panels (1 Threshold output, 2 Connected components, 3 After area filter) are squeezed into the left quarter of the slide, so every annotation inside them — the panel titles '1. Threshold output / flagged pixels (loose)', the legend 'red X = too small, rejected', and the bottom caption 'Ok = … big enough box' — renders at a few points and cannot be read from the back of a room; the panel‑3 caption also collides with the panel's bottom border and the orange bounding box. Fix: give the panel row the full left two‑thirds of the slide and ~220 px height, move all captions/legends outside the image frames into one shared legend line at body‑text size (e.g. 'white = flagged pixel • red X = component rejected as too small • yellow/orange box = kept candidate'), and put each step title above its panel in the header size.

The table contradicts the figure: it lists 'Blob 1 — cyan' as the 'largest' area and sorts it first, but in panels 2 and 3 the green blob clearly contains more pixels than the cyan one. A student comparing the picture with the table will conclude the labelling or the sort is broken. Fix: either redraw panel 3 so the cyan blob is visibly the larger one, or swap the rows so the green (top‑right) blob is Blob 1, and state the ordering you are using next to the column header.
geometry_issues: 'In plain words' (x 8.20-12.80, y 1.85-6.43 in; its text is too long for its space (about 117 words fit): shorten it to that or give the box more room, do not make the font smaller) overlaps 'Key points' (x 8.20-12.80, y 5.65-7.43 in; its text is too long for its space (about 22 words fit): shorten it to that or give the box more room, do not make the font smaller) by 4.60 x 0.78 in; move one so they do not touch.
deepseek_polish: The AREA column says only 'largest' / 'smaller' and the CENTROID column shows the placeholder '(x, y)'. Since the key point promises an area filter of 30–100,000 px, put concrete values in the table (e.g. Area 412 px / 96 px, Centroid (731, 128) / (654, 402)) so a student can see the filter actually applied.

Naming rows 'Blob 1 — cyan' and 'Blob 2 — green' makes the display colour look like real image data (the lesions are brown/yellow, not cyan/green). Use position instead — 'Blob 1 (top‑right)', 'Blob 2 (bottom)' — and add a one‑line note that colours in panel 2 are arbitrary label colours.

The 'In plain words' box is one dense 7‑line paragraph. Break it into three bullets that mirror the figure: threshold → True/False map of loose pixels; connected components → one integer label per touching group; area filter → drop specks and background, keep area + centroid + bounding box.
Say what 'touching' means (8‑connected, i.e. horizontal, vertical or diagonal neighbours), otherwise students implementing the method will not know which pixels get merged.

Panel 3's title 'area + centroid + box recorded' describes the fourth column of the story (the candidate list) but only two keeps are visible; a short caption like 'only the two large components survive, each with area, centroid and box' would tie the panel to the table below.

items.label: Slide 5 ('Method 1b: From Pixels to Candidate Blobs')
items.focus: The threshold gives scattered pixels; connected-component labelling groups them into countable blobs, and an area filter throws away noise.
deepseek_polish: The table's AREA column shows words, not areas: "largest" / "smaller". Area is the *pixel count* the filter compares against a threshold, so replace with real numbers that match the figure (e.g. Blob 1 — cyan, area 9 px; Blob 2 — green, area 6 px) and state the minimum-area threshold used (e.g. "min area = 5 px"), so a reader can see the single-pixel components (area 1 px) were the ones rejected.

Same for CENTROID: the placeholder "(x, y)" in both rows teaches nothing. Put the actual coordinates of the white dots you already draw (e.g. (287, 178) and (338, 134)) so the reader connects the dot in panel 3 to the number in the table.

Add a one-line count under the figure, e.g. "12 raw components → 2 kept, 10 rejected". The slide's stated idea is *countable* blobs; right now the reader has to count red ×s by eye to see the filter's effect.

The two bullets in the bottom-right box repeat Step 2 and the Output line word for word ("Touching flagged pixels share one label = one blob", "Keep area, centroid, bounding box — sorted largest first"). Delete that box and move its one new idea (or nothing) into the right-hand Step panel, which is currently half empty.

Because the right-hand panel has a large blank area below "Output — …", enlarge the Step text there to match the title size; it is the smallest body text on the slide and the most important explanation.

The legend says "white square = flagged pixel", but in panels 2 and 3 the flagged pixels are cyan and green. Extend the legend to "colour = the pixel's component label (one label per blob)" so the colour change between panel 1 and panel 2 doesn't look arbitrary.
Panel 1's label "Threshold output (loose flagged pixels)" is vague — say "Threshold output: raw flagged pixels, not grouped yet" so the contrast with panel 2 is explicit.

Check that each red × in panel 2 sits exactly on top of an isolated white pixel from panel 1 and that no × appears where panel 1 had no pixel; students will try to follow individual pixels across the three panels, and any mismatch breaks that.

Panel 3's yellow box around the cyan blob: make sure the white centroid dot is visible inside it (as it is for the green blob). If it is hidden among the squares, draw it on top so both kept candidates show all three outputs (area/centroid/box) consistently.

Shorten panel 3's label from "3. Candidates after filter (area, centroid, box)" to "3. Kept candidates" — the long version crowds the panel border, and the properties are already listed in the Step panel and the table.

items.label: Slide 7 ('Method 2b: Box Prompts — 'Look Inside This Rectangle'')
items.focus: A box prompt confines SAM to a region; padding then clipping makes the box generous but always inside the image.
deepseek_issues: Panel 2 shows two rectangles (dashed cyan and solid orange) but neither is labelled, so the student has to guess which is the original box and which is the padded one — that is the one thing this panel must teach. Fix: add small inline labels inside panel 2 ('own box — dashed' in cyan, 'padded box, +5 px each side' in orange) and label the gap between them '5 px'.

The symbol 'W−1' is used in the panel-3 arrow ('clipped at W−1') and again in the plain-words bar ('clamp it to the image bounds (W−1, H−1)') without ever saying what W and H are or why the minus 1 is there. Fix: define them once — 'W = image width in pixels, H = height, so the last column is W−1 (coordinates start at 0)' — and change the arrow label to 'clipped at the right image edge (W−1)'.
deepseek_polish: Panel 3 draws the lesion as a circle while panels 1–2 draw an ellipse; use the same ellipse in all three so the panels read as one box being padded and then clipped, not three different examples.

In panel 3 the lesion has almost no margin to the box, which makes it unclear why the 5 px padding overflowed. Move the lesion close to the right image edge and keep the visible ~5 px margin on the top/left/bottom so the overflow is explained by the picture.
Make the clipping visible: draw the discarded part of the padded box as a faint dashed outline inside the grey 'outside image' strip, so students see what was cut instead of having to infer it.
The small orange arrow under the padded box in panel 2 has no label; replace it with a '5 px' dimension marker between the dashed and solid edges.
'Soft edge' appears in the caption and the plain-words bar without explanation, and the drawn lesion has a hard edge — say 'the blurry lesion boundary' once so the term is defined.
Add thin arrows between panels 1 → 2 → 3 so the slide reads as a pipeline (own box → pad → clip) rather than three independent pictures.
Rename 'Own box' to 'Candidate's own box (from step 1b)' for continuity with the previous slide.

The threshold numbers in the key points ('saturation above 40', 'brightness below 30') have no stated scale, and 'saturation'/'brightness' are never defined. Add 'on a 0–255 scale' and a one-line gloss (e.g. 'saturation = how colourful the pixel is; brightness = how light it is').

The caption says every pixel left of the red line is background, but the rule on the same slide says leaf = saturation > 40 OR brightness < 30 — so a dark, low-saturation (shadow) pixel left of the line is leaf, not background. Fix by rewording the caption to 'low-saturation non-shadow pixels = background' and marking a 'shadow → also leaf' region in the histogram (or adding a small brightness histogram beneath it).

This slide repeats slide 3's three-zone template (top diagram, plain-words bottom-left, image panel bottom-right, bullet strip). items.label: Slide 12 ('Method 5a: Intersection-over-Union — Scoring a Shape')
items.focus: IoU is overlap divided by total area covered by either mask; it is 1 for a perfect match and 0 for no agreement.
deepseek_issues: The 'Empty-mask edge cases' table is wrong and contradicts the slide's own prose. Its columns are headed 'Prediction necrotic?' / 'Ground truth empty?', but the rows only make sense if both columns mean 'necrotic': 'Yes / empty-yes → 1.0' says a necrotic prediction against an empty answer key scores 1.0, and 'No / empty-yes → 0.0' says two empty masks score 0.0 — the exact opposite of the 'In plain words' text. The first row (No / No → 'area ÷ area') is 0 ÷ 0, which is undefined, not a score. Fix: head both columns 'necrotic?', make the four rows read Yes/Yes → 1.0, Yes/No → 0.0, No/Yes → 0.0, No/No → 1.0, and put a one-line footnote under the table: 'both empty = 0 ÷ 0, defined as 1.0 by convention so that agreeing on
nothing here
is not punished'.

The table is unreadable at the back of a room: the header cells are set so small that 'Prediction necrotic?' and 'Ground truth empty?' render as overlapping glyphs, and the caption 'Nothing here on both sides = perfect agreement' runs into the table's bottom border. Fix: rebuild it as a 5-row × 3-column grid at body-text size with headers wrapped onto two lines ('Prediction necrotic?' / 'Truth necrotic?' / 'IoU'), and move the caption below the panel with clear spacing.

The 'In plain words' block is a ~130-word paragraph that restates the key points and the table, and its last line is clipped at '…binarised at a threshold of 127 (values above 127' — the parenthesis never closes, so text is running off the panel. Fix: cut to two sentences — 'IoU = pixels both masks call necrotic ÷ pixels either mask calls necrotic. 1.0 = identical masks, 0.0 = no overlap; two empty masks score 1.0 so agreeing on
nothing

is rewarded.' — and move the PNG-loading detail into a single key-point line that fits, e.g. 'Ground truth: greyscale PNG, pixels > 127 = lesion, resized with nearest-neighbour so no in-between values appear.'

'Binarised above 127' and 'resized with nearest-neighbour' are unexplained implementation jargon for a beginner reading this slide alone; without a reason they are noise. Fix: keep them in the key points but attach the one-clause reason (see above) — threshold turns a grey annotation PNG into a yes/no mask; nearest-neighbour resize keeps it yes/no instead of inventing grey edge pixels.
